long_description:
***Transmutation*** **is the energetic and psycho-spiritual process of changing the nature, frequency, or purpose of an energy form within the body-mind system. Rather than suppress or release energy, the practitioner recycles and refines it, often channeling it to higher centers (chakras, glands, or awareness fields)**

Just over 20 years ago I received my Kundalini Yoga Teachers Training certification after a very challenging year. Prior to entering Teachers Training I had never actually taken a Yoga class but somehow I thought it was a good idea to go head first into what is arguably the most challenging style of Yoga. The reason Kundalini Yoga is in my opinion the most challenging style has little to do with the Asanas, or postures, taught but more to do with the incredible concentration required to properly engage a Kundalini Yoga meditation. The concentration one cultivates while practicing KY is the key to much of the extraordinary benefit one receives from a long term practice of this style...

Most of us go about our day without realizing what is happening energetically and by the end of the day we can feel rather drained. This draining of energy of course is partially due to how we expend energy throughout the day but also due to how we loose our center as the day wears on, assuming we actually know how to center ourselves in the first place. When we do a Kundalini Yoga Meditation there are many areas we place our focus. We might have our eyes on the tip of the nose, with our hands in a mudra, while chanting a precise mantra and of course all the while needing to maintain an erect spine. What all theses various point of focus does is to shunt our vital life force back into the body's central channel which will then create a powerful internal spiritual/energetic pressure which can activate the higher energy centers granting us access to our innate sensitivity, extra sensory perceptions, and deep inner peace.

Join me this week for a powerful Kundalini Yoga

long_description:
Hi Design Thinkers

The July 2026 event at DT&I, we have a special talk that brings together the concepts of Agentic AI workflows and the practical aspects of creating with AI that transforms the way you do design. Our guest speaker is [Megan Ducote](https://www.linkedin.com/in/megan-ducote-b73458113/).

*Megan is a relational technologist and design leader who builds tools for community, organizing, and civic infrastructure. She writes and speaks on decentralized technology; post-platform experiences and the future designers are positioned to shape.*

This session opens the hood on agentic workflows: moving from intent to a working tool, where you stay in the loop, where the agent runs on its own, and what the handoffs between you and the system actually look like. Not a chatbot you ask for ideas, but a way of working that produces things that run.

For a long time design has lived a few doors down from development. We hand off, we advocate, we translate. When a designer can move from intent to a working thing themselves, that distance closes, and the question of where design sits and what it's allowed to shape opens back up. The same capability raises a quieter question: once you can build almost anything, what is worth building? The work shown here leans toward the local over the extractive, the sufficient over the endlessly scaled, tools that keep people close rather than capturing them.

We look forward to seeing you at this intriguing session.

**Who would find this event useful:**

* Entrepreneurs, start-up founders
* Design / Technology professionals
* Design Strategists, design professionals
* Design and Management Students
* Community at-large

***Innovation does not happen in isolation—it grows through shared experiences, fresh perspectives, and meaningful conversations.***

🚀 Come curious. Leave inspired.

Join our Linked-in group:
https://www.linkedin.com/company/dt-i-org

DT&I Team

long_description:
We will read and respond to poetry in excruciating detail. It's fun, I promise!

We'll take turns picking a poem for us to read and respond to. Please come with at least one poem that you are ready to share—whether your own or one from another author. If you have nothing to share, feel free to listen in.

We will read each poem aloud, twice if time permits. If desired, the poem can be shared through [Proton Drive](https://drive.proton.me/urls/05PJ0BMSSW#es3lBdtVcr3y) to be shown on a laptop screen or viewed on smartphones. Paper copies can also be distributed, or feel free to just read your poem aloud---whatever you prefer works for us!

***Seattle Poetry Meetup is a proud founding member of the [Western Washington Poets Network](https://www.westernwashingtonpoetsnetwork.org/) \- check out their database of open mics and critique groups in the area\.***

VENUE

We'll start at the picnic tables east of the Community Center on the east side of Green Lake Park. We may relocate to the grass or elsewhere nearby depending on people's preference.

TRANSIT

**Bus:** your best options are probably the 45 and 62 which pass immediately east of the park and require basically no walk; the E line runs just west of the park and though it requires a bit of a hike it's pleasant walking along a paved path. See also [Seattle Transit Map](https://seattletransitmap.com/).
**Light Rail:** Roosevelt Station on the 1-Line is a 15 minute walk away coming from the east. See also [Seattle Transit Map](https://seattletransitmap.com/).
**Cycling:** Green Lake Park is encircled by a separated bike path which connects via Greenlake Dr. N to the northwest, NE Ravenna Blvd to the east, and Green Lake Way N to the south. See also the official [Bike Map](https://www.seattle.gov/transportation/projects-and-programs/programs/bike-program/bike-web-map).

long_description:
Join us for a deep-dive discussion of Middlemarch by George Eliot — widely considered one of the greatest novels ever written.
Set in a provincial English town during the 1830s, Middlemarch explores love, idealism, money, politics, status, ambition, self-delusion, and the quiet compromises that shape a life. The novel follows multiple intertwined characters, especially Dorothea Brooke and Dr. Lydgate, as they struggle between who they hoped to become and the realities of society and human nature.
This is a rich, rewarding novel that becomes more powerful the more life experience you bring to it. Expect sharp psychological insight, memorable characters, social commentary, and surprisingly modern observations about relationships and personal growth.
Length:
• Approximately 850–900 pages depending on edition
• Estimated reading time: 28–40 hours
• Recommended pace: 60–80 pages per week over 2–3 months
Perfect for readers interested in:
• Classic literature
• Human psychology
• Philosophy & ethics
• Relationships & marriage
• Social ambition & status
• Deep character studies
Bring your thoughts, favorite passages, questions, and disagreements. Even if you don’t finish the entire book, come anyway — the discussion itself will be worthwhile.
#BookClub #Middlemarch #GeorgeEliot #ClassicLiterature #LiteraryFiction #HoustonBookClub #GreatBooks #VictorianLiterature

long_description:
**Outdoor Kirtan @ Gasworks Park!**
Join us against a beautiful backdrop of the Seattle skyline as we take a journey into sacred sound meditation and mantra.

**What is Kirtan?**
Kirtan is a form of musical meditation rooted in call-and-response singing. It involves repeating simple mantras or phrases set to music, often accompanied by instruments like the harmonium, drums, and cymbals. Open to all backgrounds, kirtan offers a space for collective expression, connection, and relaxation through sound and rhythm. You don’t need to be a singer—just come with an open heart and join in at your own comfort level.

**We will meet at Bhakti Studio across the street and walk to the park together!**

**WHAT TO EXPECT**
Kirtan Soulfest is simply a transcendental party guaranteed to uplift you mentally, physically, and emotionally. The sacred mantras chanted in a call-and-response manner is the prescribed method given in the Vedas to link the inner divinity within all of us. Come with an open heart, dance and leave with an overflow of LOVE!

Mantra Meditation is a type of Sound Bath and Yoga which is an immersive experience combining powerful soundwaves and group singing/chanting to help individuals better connect with their inner selves. Yoga means to unite, Mantra Meditation will help unite your mind to your body and soul.
The sounds and singing during a Mantra Meditation session are an invitation to journey into a deeper state of consciousness as an opportunity to gain perspective on what's going on within you. The goal of the experience is to invite deep relaxation, restoration and explore self-inquiry and self-discovery.

long_description:
Are you seeking community with other like-minded women?
A space where you can be yourself, grow and become the best of yourself?

Perhaps you have desired a sisterhood where personal growth, spiritual development and empowerment is the golden thread that brings them together. Then, if that is true for you, check us out!
Welcome to the Sacred Sisterhood – CSLDallas Women’s Circle. Here, we embrace women from all walks of life, stages, ages, races, cultures, and religious traditions. We are seekers, heart-centered, and yearning for something more.
Since ancient times, women have gathered in circles to share stories, celebrate, support each other, and forge bonds with their sisters, embodying our Oneness with Life and each other.

In this sacred space, our purpose is to love and transform ourselves while also transforming the world through connections and nourishing friendships. Through deep listening and understanding, we create an opportunity for growth in a spirit of equality and acceptance. When we feel seen, heard, and held, we can transcend current conditions and embrace our true radiance and power as magic happens.
Join us each month as we journey together towards love, transformation, and in a sisterhood of unity.
What you can expect from the group:

* Utilizing monthly themes, we will explore topics important to women through dialogue, active listening, journaling and spiritual principles and practices, grounded in the Science of Mind.
* From honoring our roles in the world – daughter, sister, mother, grandmother, aunt, and friend – we will share wisdom as well as stories of how women are the nurturers, gatherers and leaders working to transform our world. How can we make a difference?
* Celebrations, rituals, and gatherings – We will ‘lunch’ together once a quarter

When we meet:
We meet the 2nd Saturday of each month from 10am to noon in person at CSLDallas. In coming months, we may add or alternate with a virtual meeting.
The Sacred Sisterhood Leader – Deni

long_description:
Our NEIGHBORHOOD GEMS series features emblematic meals from around the world. This series shines a light on local restaurants and is designed to bring together inquisitive foodies and dishes that are unique and oh so worth a trip on roads less traveled!

Join us for brunch with a Latin twist at all-day Rosa's Diner!

**From Eater DC**

After going dark for two years, a tony corner of downtown D.C. makes a comeback today, Friday, May 22, as Rosa's Diner, an all-day ode to Americana classics with Latin twists.

The glamorous Victorian row house attached to the Moxy hotel was restored to its original glory back in 2023 to welcome Atlas Restaurant Group's polished oyster bar Parlor Victoria, which didn’t last long.

The brick-framed building’s latest culinary chapter falls under the watch of executive chef Francisco Pomalaza, who’s cooked in New York, Chicago, and his hometown of Miami – but never before in D.C. His newest post in a 9-to-5 corridor is a big departure from his recent beachside gig at Florida’s Havana Beach Bar & Grill at the Pearl Hotel.

“I felt that this was more freedom for creativity. There are so many countries to touch on,” says Pomalaza, who’s Peruvian. “It’s still an American theme, but influenced by Latin flavors.”

See: his eggs “Benedict” – which is actually a pupusa topped with beef birria and aji amarillo hollandaise.

Unlike its short-lived predecessor, which served seafood towers and steaks in an opulent setting, Rosa’s Diner dresses things down a bit with retro bar stools, slick green booths, and a walk-up counter with a full coffee program and a case stocked with its house-made pastries. A full bar spotlights spirits like a Latin gin made from Malbec grapes.

long_description:
Curious how to start learning something? Want to chat with someone of another discipline? Need a place to work on a project and share it with others? ISG is a social, game development focused work group that encourages people of all skill levels and disciplines to come together and collaborate for the benefit of all.

This is a great place to begin your game development journey and learn from fellow game creators as they work on their projects.

**Bring your laptop** and any software you will need to work on your game/art/music.

How it Works:

• Show up, introduce yourself, let everyone know what you hope to accomplish

• Ask for help with anything, get to know others, share your projects, or enjoy the company of others as you work!

• Share your highs and lows, high fives all around

***

How to find us:
It can be kind of hard to find us! We are on the 4th floor of the Armory building. Follow the signs to the restrooms, and nearby you'll find the stairs and the elevator. Take one of those to the fourth floor and look for the Seattle Indies banner.

***

Accessibility information:
There is paid street parking all around the neighborhood. There are paid parking garages at 516 Harrison St, 650 3rd Ave N, and at the corner of 5th Ave N and Harrison St. The Seattle Center has nearby bus stops serviced by the 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 13, 15, 17, 18, 19, 24, 32, 33, D Line, and the monorail. The venue is listed as wheelchair accessible. The Seattle Center has additional accessibility information available on their website here: http://www.seattlecenter.com/about/accessibility.aspx

If you are coming by Light Rail it is best to get off at Westlake Station and then ride the Monorail over to the Seattle Center which drops you off right at the Armory.

***

Seattle Indies strives to be an inclusive and welcoming community for everyone. By attending our events, you are agreeing to follow our code of conduct (https://www.seattleindies.org/code-of-conduct/).

long_description:
Join us at the weekly Kirtan and in celebrating all current month's birthdays!

Welcome, please join our community for call and response Kirtan & Chai, chanting mantras and devotional songs.

Kirtan is immediately after the weekly SoundBath & Prana Lifeforce Healing (430pm-530pm). It is for everyone, participate or just enjoy the energy / rhythms.

Welcome to bring, but not required, a vegan/vegetarian dish to share for social after the Kirtan.

What is Kirtan:
Kirtan is the Yoga of Devotion (Bhakti Yoga). Derived from a Sanskrit root meaning to call, recite, praise, or glorify, put simply, kirtan is the act of praising and glorifying the Divine.

Why Kirtan:
Chanting Kirtan is a devotional practice that helps to uplift the mind, open the heart and bring inner peace. It is the fastest, easiest and most joyful way to achieve peace of mind. The mantras are mystical universal sounds that resonate with our chakras and remove negative energies. So, it is important that we chant so that we can benefit from this powerful healing energy.

Game days have 3 segments. **You do not need to come for the whole day!** However, if you are testing your own game you should stay and test at least one other designer's game as well.

**OPEN PLAY TESTING** 2:00pm - 3:00 pm
This is unstructured play time, ideal for very short games (20min or less), or games requiring 1-2 players. If you're a designer check in with me and then grab an available table and let people know you are looking for players. If you're a player, just sit down at a game and play!

**SESSION ONE** 3:15pm - 4:15pm
**SESSION TWO** 4:30pm - 6:30pm
Scheduled sessions are the core of First Play! There is a 1 hour session and a 2 hour session. Before each session designers will be asked to give an 'elevator pitch' of their game, after which players can decide which game they want to play. Sessions are ideal for games that are 20-90 minutes. After play, be sure to leave time to give and receive feedback!

Welcome to the first gathering of Desi Men’s Circle NJ!

Let’s meet, make new friends, and start building a supportive community for South Asian men in New Jersey.

Whether you’ve been in the U.S. for years or recently arrived, this is an opportunity to connect with others who may share similar experiences and challenges.

There is no formal agenda and no pressure to speak. Come as you are.

Topics may include:

* Making friends as adults
* Career and professional growth
* Immigration experiences
* Family and cultural expectations
* Fitness and health
* Relationships
* Life in New Jersey

Our goal is simple: create genuine friendships and a strong sense of community.

All South Asian men and those who identify with South Asian culture are welcome.

long_description:
Beginning at the **Contemporary Arts Museum**, today's walk is miles of shady trails and streets through the **Rice University-Hermann Park** area. The large old trees that give the area its character come as no accident, fitting nicely into an earlier generation of urban design. The lower end of south Main was rural in the early 1910s, and the donation of land for **Hermann Park** at the same time as the founding of the **Rice Institute** in **1912** allowed the entire area to be laid out according to the grand principles of the [City Beautiful Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Beautiful_movement). **Wide boulevards** and **esplanades** through out that part of town all reflect the popular ideas that beautiful cities with **grand public spaces** for **fountains, museums, reflecting pools, and parks** are better for uplifting citizens. Popular in America from the 1890s through the early 20th century, it is a contrast to the cul-de-sac culture of the decades to come.

Wear comfortable shoes and bring plenty of water. The heat in Texas is always a concern so let someone know if you are having a hard time. For more information about hiking check out this very useful hiking website: [HATS and More site](https://www.hatsandmore.org/)

CHAT GPT guesses about what Houston will look like in a thousand years. [The trees dont look like they have kept up....](https://www.houstonchronicle.com/news/houston-texas/trending/article/skyline-houston-in-the-future-ai-image-generator-18108698.php)

Our organizers are not guides nor do we have any special training. We are here to come up with hiking ideas and get the hike started. Take the same precautions you would if hiking alone, including the fitness needed to make long hikes. Then enjoy the hike among friends.

COVID PRECAUTIONS:
Bring and wear a mask when not hiking and follow the best practices to prevent the transmission of COVID.

**Gathering Place:**
In front of the
Contemporary Arts Museum
5216 Montrose Boulevard,

**KIRTAN: Cosmic Chanting & Meditation with Dave & Kim‑Shri Maurischat** **Sunday, July 12 • 12:30–2:00 PM** **Center for Spiritual Living San José** **1195 Clark Street, San José, CA 95125** **Love Offering Appreciated**
There are moments when the heart longs for something deeper — a way to reconnect with the Divine through sound, breath, and shared presence. This Kirtan experience with Dave and Kim‑Shri Maurischat offers exactly that: a sacred doorway into joy, devotion, and inner stillness.
Kirtan is an ancient practice of **call‑and‑response chanting**, where voices blend into a single vibration of love and remembrance. As the music builds, something beautiful happens — the mind softens, the heart opens, and a sense of unity fills the room.
During this immersive experience, you will:

* **Experience the bliss of chanting the names of the Divine Beloved**, carried by harmonium, drum, and the collective voice of the community
* **Be guided through gentle hatha yoga stretches** to prepare the body for chanting and meditation
* **Settle into a natural flow of meditative awareness**, supported by these timeless devotional practices

Whether you are brand‑new to chanting or a longtime lover of sacred sound, this gathering will meet you exactly where you are. **All are welcome.**
**Center for Spiritual Living San José** **1195 Clark Street, San José, CA 95125**

long_description:
**Mysore Style Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga**
Mysore Style Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga is named after the city in South India; Mysore where this transformative practice originated from the co-founders Krishnamacharya & K. Pattabhi Jois nearly 90 years ago. Mysore style means you work at your own pace while the teacher provides tailored instruction from giving postures, asking questions, & giving hands-on adjustments when necessary. The beauty of Mysore is you don’t need to keep up with the teacher or other students in the room since it is an individual practice similar to an individual playing a song on a guitar, doing a dance or doing a kata in martial arts in a customized way. Since the same postures are repeated each time you can memorize the sequence giving you practice to take home with you or wherever you roam on Mother Earth.
Bio:
Shane has had daily Mysore yoga practice for nearly 20 years. He practiced and studied with/ Master teachers in North America & India including Richard Freeman, Mary Taylor, Rolf Naujokat, & Marci Naujokat. Shane has had a daily yoga practice since 2003 & has been teaching yoga since 2004.

description:

**Join us in a discussion about the book** **"Man's Search for Meaning" by Viktor Frankl!**

The book club also now has a Discord server! Feel free to join to keep up the discussion between meetups! [l](https://discord.gg/EnrvhBMZ)

You don't have to buy anything, but the venue has light pub fare, ice cream, and a great selection of both alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. They also allow outside restaurant food, so bring something to eat if you need sustenance!

**Book Description:**

This seminal book, which has been called “one of the outstanding contributions to psychological thought” by Carl Rogers and “one of the great books of our time” by Harold Kushner, has been translated into more than fifty languages and sold over sixteen million copies. “An enduring work of survival literature,” according to the New York Times, Viktor Frankl’s riveting account of his time in the Nazi concentration camps, and his insightful exploration of the human will to find meaning in spite of the worst adversity, has offered solace and guidance to generations of readers since it was first published in 1946. At the heart of Frankl’s theory of logotherapy (from the Greek word for “meaning”) is a conviction that the primary human drive is not pleasure, as Freud maintained, but rather the discovery and pursuit of what the individual finds meaningful. Today, as new generations face new challenges and an ever more complex and uncertain world, Frankl’s classic work continues to inspire us all to find significance in the very act of living, in spite of all obstacles.

Within the Chicago Psychedelic Buddhism Meetup group, we had been talking for a long time about creating a monthly integration group. We are hosting the sixteenth meeting for that purpose! This time we're meeting on a weeknight and it will be inside a private residence. We'll also have a potluck for anyone who wants to participate (but not required to bring food). Join us for our weekly Indian dance class and step into the diverse, enchanting world of Indian dance and cinema. In this class, you will learn fun, feel-good choreographies to hit songs from Bollywood, and other regional film industries such as Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam.

The choreographies will be a lively blend of folk (Kuthu, Bhangra, Garba), western, and semi-classical dance styles, celebrating the rich variety of Indian movement and expression. One of the most beautiful aspects of Indian “filmy” dance is its ability to transcend boundaries, with no strict rules or restrictions, making it accessible and enjoyable for everyone.

long_description:
**Welcome to Bhakti Night** \- an evening dedicated to the wisdom and practice of *bhakti-yoga*.

The evening begins with a soul-stirring *kirtan*, a musical form of meditation, where the air will resonate with melodious chants and the rhythmic beats of traditional instruments. As the sweet sound vibrations fill the room, you'll find your heart opening up, and any stress or worries gently dissipate, replaced by a profound sense of peace and contentment. The *kirtan* is followed by a talk on teachings from the ancient yoga tradition which is always thought provoking and even entertaining!

As the night draws to a close, we'll conclude with a delightful vegetarian dinner. Savor the sanctified dishes, lovingly prepared with devotion, and experience how food can be an offering of love and nourishment for the soul.

Whether you are a seasoned practitioner or a curious newcomer, this program promises an evening filled with spiritual bliss and inner harmony. We look forward to sharing this wonderful journey of devotion with you!

Save Kelp, Eat Urchin!
Join us at sunrise for a sea urchin foraging class, where we will help remove some of the overgrown sea urchin population - so we can eat it! We will teach you how to open and enjoy this incredible delicacy. You may have heard it called “uni” in a sushi restaurant, but it’s SO much tastier when it’s fresh. Take home up to 35 urchin - if you can carry that much! Learn how humans can be a helping hand to restore balance to ecosystems impacted by climate change.

July 15, 6am-9:30am
Sonoma Coast, California
All registrations must be completed on our website [here](https://www.forkinthepath.org/registration-urchin)

#### What You Will Learn

We're thrilled to bring you to the ocean to forage for sea urchins on the gorgeous Sonoma Coast.
This 3-hour class is all about sea urchins or uni, as you may have heard it called in a sushi restaurant. Learn where they live, what they eat, and who eats them...but more specifically, who hasn't been eating them and how that has impacted our kelp forests, and how humans eating them actually lends a helping hand to bringing our intertidal zone back into balance!
Take home up to 35 urchins. You'll have a deeper understanding of how some of our ocean habitats are the first major biomes to experience sudden collapse due to a rapidly changing climate, and how we can mitigate the damage.

#### **Where**

A beach in Northern Sonoma, about 2.5 hours north of San Francisco. Exact location provided with registration.

**More Important Details**
These programs are very popular and often fill up very quickly. We encourage you to register right away if you'd like to attend! If you are reading this, the class is not full. Space is updated daily.

long_description:
📍 **Ciao Caffe, Windsor, ON**
📅 **Wednesday, July 15, 2026, at 8:00 PM EDT**

Want to **really** challenge yourself in **American Sign Language**? Then **Salon: ASL** is where you belong. This isn’t just a meetup—it’s a space designed for signers of all skill levels to **learn, sharpen, and immerse** themselves in ASL through real conversations and community connection.

**Salon is more than a practice session—it’s an experience.** Here, fluent signers refine their skills, setting the standard for others to follow. Beginners step into an authentic ASL space, learning through immersion while respecting the flow of communication. And **together**, we create a space that bridges gaps and builds connections with the Deaf community.

### How it Works:

🖐️ **The Challenge:** One hour of **pure ASL conversation—no speaking, no English.** Writing is allowed.
💬 **The Debrief:** In the last 30 minutes, we open up for questions, clarifications, and deeper learning.
👀 **The Experience:** Watch, engage, absorb. Beginners are welcome—but silence and observation are key.

Stepping out of your comfort zone is how true learning happens. **Push yourself, embrace the challenge, and take your ASL skills further than ever.**

🔥 Ready to give it a try? Join us at **Salon: ASL**—where signers grow and the language thrives.

Volunteers of all cultures are welcome. Help cook and share a meal with Native American seniors at St. Kateri Center. We will cook both cultural relevant food for Indians (maze, beans, squash, wild rice, bison, fry bread, etc.) and popular American lunch items. This is a recurring event on the third Thursday of every month.

Both experienced and non experienced volunteers are welcome. All cooking and plating instructions will be provided on site and it is easy. All volunteers must be 14 years or older. Minors must get their parents' or legal guardians' permission to participate.

Volunteers will meet at St. Kateri Center, next to St. Benedict Church

3938 N Leavitt St, Chicago, IL 60618

We will start cooking at 9 am and be ready to serve by noon. We will cook 40 to 80 meals to serve on site and pack some meals for home delivery. Volunteers will meet in the kitchen. The shift time is flexible. If you have to come later or leave early, that's OK.

Please dress appropriately to work in a kitchen. Wear closed toe shoes with non slip bottoms, like sneakers. Slacks, jeans or long pants. No shorts or tank tops allowed. You will be asked to wear a hair net or you can bring a baseball cap or hat to manage your hair. You can also bring your own apron if you own one.

There is free street parking in the area, usually on the same street or the next block. It is also near CTA bus routes.

This talk explores Nguyen's multidisciplinary practice and creative process.

[REGISTER HERE](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/artist-talk-maya-nguyen-tickets-1989924015297)

Join us for an artist talk by Maya Nguyen, whose exhibition LATERAL ENTRANT is currently on view at the Goethe-Institut Chicago.
*Light refreshments will be served. Please [register](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/artist-talk-maya-nguyen-tickets-1989924015297) in advance and bring a state- or federally-issued photo ID for check-in in the 150 N. Michigan building lobby.*

**ABOUT THE ARTIST**
**Maya Nguyen** is an interdisciplinary artist with a focus on sound and diasporic making. Marked by migration from Hanoi, to Moscow, and now Chicago, her practice develops formal strategies to articulate experiences of lived ambiguity. Nguyen incorporates disparate (and often clashing) material sources into forms that remain conceptually indeterminate, such as performance-lectures, sound improvisation, and collaborative sculptures. Some favored materials include: speech fragments, mistranslations, body glitches, migratory routes, urban recordings, sounds imitating nature sounds, internet debris, baby babble, breast pump parts, and videos of daily life, among others. Her works are presented internationally, moving fluidly between galleries, sound venues, pop-up shows and universities, with recent shows at Watershed Art & Ecology (Chicago), Jack Straw New Media Gallery (Seattle), Zentrum für Kunst und Urbanistik (Berlin), Saari Residency (Mynämäki, FI), Manzi Art Space (Hanoi), and recognition as Arts Club of Chicago Fellow 2025-26 and Karl Sczuka Radio Art Research Prize 2024 (SWR/Goethe Institute). Nguyen holds a BA in Philosophy/Comparative Literature from The University of Chicago and MFA in Sound from The School of the Art Institute of Chicago.

long_description:

long_description:
**Please see photo of where parking is, if parking north of Memorial, the pedestrian bridge is straight across Memorial from Water Works.**

**If late, see in photo the direction we take off in.**

**I’m 832 600 4678. Can’t guarantee I’ll have signal or hear it.**

**Park at Buffalo Bayou Visitor Center - The Waterworks and Cistern plaza, 105 Sabine, or across pedestrian bridge on North Memorial Way.**

**Sadly, the cool 1950’s futuristic design of the restaurants and shops under Bank of the Southwest (now Travis Tower) building has been remodeled into blandness.**

**Hard to get a signal and track miles, so we’ll go for time, will try to make it two hours.**
**We walk a bit along the bayou and enter tunnels near Hobby Center. Lots of food and all the shops you would need to support a city of office workers.**

**We’ll walk through many different old and new building styles. We pass by the Hyatt lobby if anyone wants to go in. I try to stick to interesting parts but there will be long mostly empty stretches.**

**We go through the Understory, food and drink area and go in a wonderful old classic bank lobby with historic murals. I would like for us to at least go in the beautiful 100 year old Julia Ideson Library Building, next to City Hall.**

**Just regular clothes, don’t really need hiking/walking gear, we’ll be outside only a short bit, of course water, restrooms, etc in tunnels.**

**No dogs.**

HOW IT WORKS : We will try to assign tables for each represented languages and will direct attendees to their respective tables accordingly. All languages are welcome! However we don't guarantee the availability of a partner in that particular language, you would like to exchange.

Rules to abide :

## **Urban Reset La Dera Park: Walking Meditation & Movement**

**Hosted by Monique Marie \| The Free Spirit Yogi**

### **From "Doing" into "Being"**

In the heart of the city lies a pocket of peace. Join us at **Ladera Park** for an intimate, guided journey designed to help you shed the noise of the week and return to your center. This isn't just a yoga class; it’s a curated experience of stillness, nature, and community.

### **The Experience**

Our reset is divided into four intentional phases:

* **The Silent Walk (40 Minutes):** We begin at our meeting spot with a single chime of the singing bowl. You will receive a **Mindful Focus Card**—a tactile, hand-held guide to anchor your thoughts as you wander toward the oaks. Every few minutes, the chime will ring again, calling you to take one deep, conscious breath, notice exactly where you are, and continue your journey in silence.
* **The Movement (35 Minutes):** Once we reach the dappled shade of the oak grove, we transition from the internal journey to the physical. We will move through a grounding yoga flow designed to integrate the peace of your walk into your body.
* **The Integration (5 Minutes):** We conclude our journey by bringing the stillness of the park into the center of our being. As we settle into our final resting pose, the "doing" is officially done. This is your time to absorb the frequency of the trees, the rhythm of your breath, and the shift in your energy.
* The play. Lets challenge our balance by trying arm balances, inversions and new asanas to deepen our practice.
* The departure. One final collective breath to share gratitude.

### **What’s Provided**

To ensure you can remain fully "hands-free" and present, we provide:

* **Yoga Mat Backpacks:** To ensure you can fully immerse yourself in the walking meditation, we provide complimentary use of our Yoga Mat Backpacks for the duration of the experience.

long_description:
Hey Poetry Lovers!

This group is on a roll. Here’s the gist:

We meet at the **Capital One Café in Chinatown** from **12pm - 2pm** every other week.

For enrichment, we start by reading and reflecting on a **“published poem”**, suggested by someone in the group. No advance preparation is necessary. But feel free to check out some of the poems we’ve read [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSyE_wCLQCPHRrKmN5F9tOIeeRQUZESxjRXGVBoCF2uU8Gm0_d0uECiCBCQXEy6ksxfsBOhtRIOpW3T/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true&widget=true&headers=false%22%3E%3C/iframe%3E). Or submit suggestions for future meetings [here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSexGc2Z2Kp6bZW0D3_hfJ7NUUkfNHf7TXX-43FglCeBd9EF2Q/viewform?usp=send_form).

Next, we **share our work and offer feedback**. Depending on attendance, everyone gets \~10 minutes to use as they like. (No need to share, though; you’re welcome to come even if you prefer just to listen.)

We maintain a **Discord server** to help share our work and communicate outside our bi-weekly meet-ups. If you haven’t used Discord before, take a moment to download it and create an account before arriving. When we meet you on Saturday, we will add you to our server, the “DC Poetry Workshop”, and can help you navigate the app if you have questions.

Finally, if you plan on sharing a poem, consider how you will do so. Some options include:

* Print 5-10 copies to distribute in person
* Take and share screenshots in the Discord chat.
* Copy the poem into a google doc, change sharing settings to “anyone with link”, and copy the google doc link into the Discord chat.

Most importantly, we’re excited to meet you!

Catch you on Saturday,

Diego / Ian / Cayden / Nate / Otasha / Lia / An

**Note that each week we will be reading from texts that fall outside the formally published texts from ACA.**

**The Power of the Meeting**
**At the heart of ACA is our commitment to meeting with one another. We understand that recovery cannot happen in isolation. By coming together, we:**

* **Learn and grow using inspiring literature**
* **Practice new behaviors leading to happier, more functional lives**
* **Develop and hone essential relationship skills**
* **Find safe environments to work through lifelong issues**
* **Heal through connection with others who share similar experiences**

long_description:
Within each of us lies a dream that carries us toward Africa. Whether it began in childhood or later in life, the image of the savanna, snow-capped mountains, and untamed wildlife stirs curiosity, emotion, and the desire for adventure. Kilimanjaro, the rooftop of the African continent, is the symbol of that call — a legendary mountain, a natural wonder that seems lifted from an African fairytale. With its imposing silhouette surrounded by tropical forests and arid savannas, Kilimanjaro offers a one-of-a-kind experience — a journey from equatorial jungle to a landscape resembling the polar tundra.

It's an ascent that leaves a mark not only physically but emotionally. As you climb, you don't just reach a summit — you rediscover a part of yourself. The peak offers a new horizon: clearer, broader, and more confident.

From a technical standpoint, Kilimanjaro is the most accessible peak of the famous Seven Summits and Seven Volcanoes. It doesn't require mountaineering skills and is successfully climbed each year by people of all ages — from 6 to 83 years old. The trails are well-maintained, logistics are excellent, and porters carry most of the gear, making the experience both comfortable and achievable.

For those who want to extend their African journey, the expedition can be followed by a spectacular safari in Tarangire and Ngorongoro — the land of great migrations, lions, and elephants, an unmatched natural spectacle.

This is more than just a vacation — it's a journey that leaves a deep mark on your soul and gently changes the way you see the world.

Highlights:
• Uhuru Peak (5,895m) – Roof of Africa
• Journey from tropical rainforest to arctic-alpine zone
• Machame Route – one of the most scenic paths
• Sunrise summit attempt under a star-filled sky
• Certificate of achievement upon completion
• Optional: Safari extension in Tarangire and Ngorongoro Crater

description:

long_description:
Socrates Cafés are gatherings around the world where people from different backgrounds get together and exchange thoughtful ideas and experiences while embracing the Socratic Method; the idea that we learn more when we question, and question with others.
Although this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Those attending decide upon the questions of the night. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, moral issues, and the first principles of things.

Prior to each meeting we vote online for the questions we will discuss. That way, we will have enough time to ruminate on them and have more in-depth conversations. If you RSVP to a meeting, you may post your question in the event comments section below. I'll send out a survey for voting a few days prior to the meetup. We discuss two questions each night. So you will get to cast two votes in the survey.
When we meet, we break into smaller groups of five to seven to discuss the top two vote-getters. Each group discusses one question for around 45-50 minutes, and we then take a short break. After reconvening, each group moves on to its second question.

Hope to see you there!

-Brian

long_description:
**Q: What is this “Great Films Project” thing?**
A: It’s an opportunity for in-depth conversation about the greatest films ever made. Each month, we’ll be discussing and analyzing three acclaimed films. This July those films will be "8&1/2", "Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans", and "The Searchers").

**Q: How is this different than your regular monthly topic-driven Meetups?**
A: Think of it a little more like a book club. We want to do deep dives into these films and may spend an hour or more dissecting each one (which is why we’re limiting to three). Because we want to truly engage with these films, we’re asking that all attendees come in familiar with them and have strong opinions, stimulating questions and enthusiasm to engage and discover.

**Q: Hold on! Who’s to say what the “greatest films ever made” are? Isn’t that subjective?**
A: Of course, and opinions on why a film should or should not be considered such will be very up for discussion. But there has long been and evolving “film canon” set over the years by critics, film scholars and cinephiles. We are using the Top 1,000 Greatest Films list from the “They Shoot Pictures, Don't They?” website ([https://theyshootpictures.com/](https://theyshootpictures.com/))

**Q: So, what’s so great about this list?**
A: It's not just one list. It’s an annual aggregation of "best-of" film lists from almost 11,000 individual lists by critics, filmmakers, publications, and websites. TSPDT is critic-driven. It prioritizes historical influence, artistic innovation, and critical consensus. That doesn’t mean we will all agree with the rankings, but we think it’s a good place to start.

**Q: What movies are coming up? What will this monthly “project” look like over time?**
A: That’s an easy one. Just go to the TSPDT top 1,000 list ([https://theyshootpictures.com/gf1000_all1000films_table.php](https://theyshootpictures.com/gf1000_all1000films_table.php)) and check out the first 36 titles. Those are the films we’ll cover over a year,

[Profs and Pints DC](https://www.profsandpints.com/washingtondc) presents: **“Designing Belonging,”** on the messages sent by various institutional environments and how they can be made more welcoming, with Martha Kakooza, research associate in the department of higher education and student affairs at Morgan State University, where she teaches courses on gender, sexuality, and narrative and qualitative research.

[Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/dc-designing-belonging](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/dc-designing-belonging) .]

Why do some rooms make people relax while others make them stiffen? Why do certain workplaces, schools, restaurants, churches, airports, and waiting rooms seem to say, “you are welcome here,” while others quietly signal “this was not built with you in mind”?

Explore how ordinary spaces shape belonging at a talk that will offer guidance to those seeking to create inclusive environments for students, clients, and customers. Being on hand will help anyone out there sort out why some environments have felt so welcoming while others left them focused on exits.

You’ll learn how a room's layout, lighting, seating, signage, sound, artwork, security presence, and history all affect whether people feel at ease or on edge, powerful or invisible, cared for or merely processed. People read these cues almost instantly, usually before they can explain why a place feels welcoming or alienating.

Dr. Martha Kakooza, a scholar whose research has focused space, identity, and institutional environments, will discuss why the same environment can feel like home to one person and like a closed door to another. She’ll describe how experiences of race, culture, class, gender, age, disability, and migration all shape how we read a space. We’ll look at how no space is truly neutral, because each one carries social messages and histories.

**Designers**: Grab a purple name badge, demo your game, get quality feedback, and improve your game design project!

**Playtesters**: Grab an orange name badge, play interesting, work-in-progress games, and help them on their journey to be pitched, published, or crowdfunded!

This is a casual event, there's no set schedule. Play a game, give/get great feedback, and do it again, while enjoying great food and good vibes.

Ask the organizer(s) if you have any questions, we're here to help!

long_description:
**RSVP via:**
https://app.gistirl.com/event-details/BpsprJ25dWQvNJGDoEhC
**Early Bird Discounts | More $ Later**

Hey night market fans!

Come soak in the glow of the string lights, the smell of sizzling street food, and the heavy bass of live beats right by the dance floor. Join me for an easy evening where we spend the first hour chatting one-on-one through the Gist IRL app, and then head out in small groups to grab some food, dance to Bhangra beats, and make some real connections along the way.

We'll kick things off with fast, friendly conversations. The app handles all the pairings, so you always know exactly who you're talking to and can just focus on breaking the ice with folks from all different backgrounds. Once we wrap up the rounds, you'll select the people you vibed with the most, and we'll group up to dive into the night market.

By the time you hit the dance floor, you've already got a fun crew to share the street food and live beats with. We'll be splitting into groups of 4-6, giving you a ready-made squad to grab some spicy skewers or a cold drink before migrating to the music. Whether these guys become your go-to night market and dancing squad or it's just a fantastic evening out under the stars, you're going to have a blast.

The Plan:

- 6:00PM: Check-In. Follow the link to set up your quick profile on your phone.
- 6:05PM - 7:25PM: One-on-One Rounds. The app pairs you up for some fun, focused chats. Find out who shares your love for vibrant cultural festivals, pulsing Punjabi beats, and delicious global street food.
- 7:25PM+: Group Up & Explore. Reconnect with the people you clicked with, form a tight crew of 4-6, grab some food from the trucks, snag a drink from the outdoor bars, and head over to the dance floor together.

This FREE event will transform Yerba Buena Gardens, Jessie Square, and Yerba Buena Lane into an open-air festival of music, dance, food, and community. long_description:
Join us on July 25 at Sarva in Back Bay as we discuss *The Loneliness of Sonia & Sunny* by Kiran Desai.

Nearly twenty years after winning the Booker Prize for *The Inheritance of Loss*, Kiran Desai returns with an ambitious novel that spans continents, generations, and cultures. At its heart is the story of Sonia and Sunny, two young Indians whose lives intersect between India and the United States as they search for love, purpose, and a sense of belonging in an increasingly globalized world. What begins as a chance encounter unfolds into a sweeping exploration of family, identity, migration, class, and the ties that connect us across time and distance.
Desai's novel is both an intimate love story and an expansive family saga, filled with vivid characters, sharp observations, and reflections on what it means to build a life between cultures. Through Sonia and Sunny's journeys, the novel examines loneliness not simply as isolation, but as a universal human experience shaped by history, family expectations, and the search for connection.

As always, our discussion will be relaxed, welcoming, and accompanied by excellent food. Whether you read every page, are still making your way through this doorstopper of a novel, or are simply curious about contemporary South Asian literature, we'd love to have you join us.
📖 Book: *The Loneliness of Sonia & Sunny* by Kiran Desai
📍 Location: Sarva, Back Bay
📅 Date: July 25
Come for the fiction, stay for the food and conversation.

# Hindustani Classical Music

### [SF Donation/Free Meditation & Mindfulness Classes](https://www.meetup.com/san-francisco-mindfulness-meetup/)

## Details

There are evenings that stay with you long after the last note has faded.
This is one of them.

Join us for an evening of Hindustani classical vocal music with **Swati Jhaveri** — a journey through ragas that span the breadth of human emotion, from the profound and contemplative to the tender and joyful.
The program moves through the classical tradition with intention and heart: from the weight of a full-throated khayal to the playful intimacy of a thumri, and culminating in an original composition that reflects Swati's own voice within the lineage she carries.

Trained in the Indore and Mewati gharana traditions, Swati brings to the stage a rare ability to hold depth and warmth in equal measure.

She will be accompanied by **Tushar Gupte on tabla** and **Satyam Bagwe on harmonium**.
An evening of music in its most honest form.
**Swati Jhaveri** pursues music with a deep passion. She is currently under the guidance of Pandit Hemang Mehta (disciple of Padma Vibhushan Pandit Jasraj and Pandit Chandrasekhar Swamy) of the Mewati Gharana and Vidushi Kankana Banerjee of the Indore and Mewati Gharana (disciple of Ustad Amir Khan Sahib and Pandit Pratap Narayan) as part of the guru shishya parampara.
Swati started learning music at the age of 4 and has had the opportunity to study with many learned gurus including Pandit Pratap Narayan, Pandit Askaran Sharma, and Pandit Sougata Banerjee.

She started a non profit called “Swara Institute for Music Research and Appreciation” with the purpose of improving the reach of Indian Classical music through teaching, content creation, and supporting under-privileged, retired, and upcoming musicians.

Swati has produced a series of classical singles with a contemporary touch on popular platforms, in an attempt to make classical music palatable to wider masses and our younger generat

Celebrate the 22nd anniversary of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in the Detroit area, beautifully coinciding with India's Independence Day.

This grand celebration will feature:

- **2:00 PM** – Vedic Mahapuja (sacred fire ceremony)
- **2:00 – 5:00 PM** – Annakut Darshan (offering of hundreds of food items to the deities)
- **4:00 PM** – Patotsav Sabha (cultural assembly with addresses by visiting swamis)

The Patotsav marks the sacred anniversary of the mandir's murti pratishtha (consecration of the deities) and is one of the most auspicious events of the year.

**Details:**
- Date: Saturday, August 15, 2026
- Location: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Canton, MI
- Admission: Free and open to all

Special prasad and celebrations throughout the day. All families welcome.

The 51st edition takes runners on a spectacular tour of Washington DC — past the Pentagon, along the Potomac, through Georgetown, around the National Mall, and past the Capitol. Registration opens April 6.

title: BMW Dallas Marathon 2026
description: Dallas's premier marathon weekend with full marathon, half, ultra, 5K, and relay options. Benefits Scottish Rite for Children.
long_description: The BMW Dallas Marathon has been a Texas running tradition for over 40 years. The race weekend features a full marathon, half marathon, ultra marathon, 5-person relay, 10K, and 5K — something for every runner. The course starts at Dallas City Hall, loops through scenic White Rock Lake, and finishes back downtown. Since 1997, the marathon has donated nearly $5 million to Scottish Rite for Children. The December timing provides cool running weather, and the event has sold out three consecutive years.
venue_info: Start/finish at Dallas City Hall, 1500 Marilla St. The course is flat and fast, passing through downtown Dallas and around White Rock Lake (120m total elevation gain). DART light rail serves the City Hall area. Post-race party with food, beer, and live music.
